# The g-code file's header and source block

Every g-code file plymeld writes starts with a header and ends with a source block. Both are comment lines, so a
printer skips them. This page is their format, for tools that read them.

Every line below starts with `; ` (semicolon, space). In the patterns, capitals stand for values; everything else is
written exactly as shown.

## The header

The first lines of the file. Its layout depends on the machine.

### Most machines

```
; generated by plymeld VERSION
; total layer number: LAYERS
```

The machine's start code follows.

### Flashforge machines (the Creator 5)

The layout these printers read for their screen:

```
; HEADER_BLOCK_START
; generated by plymeld VERSION
; total layer number: LAYERS
; filament_diameter: MM[,MM...]
; max_z_height: MM
; filament: 1[,2...]
; HEADER_BLOCK_END

; filament used [mm] = MM[, MM...]
; filament used [cm3] = CM3[, CM3...]
; <filament id="N" type="KIND" color="#RRGGBB" used_m="M" />
; total filament change = CHANGES
; total layers count = LAYERS
; estimated printing time (normal mode) = DURATION
; estimated first layer printing time (normal mode) = DURATION
```

- There is one `<filament .../>` line per filament, numbered from 1. `type` and `color` are left out when the config
  does not give them.
- Lists hold one entry per filament, in that order.
- `DURATION` is written as `1h 2m 3s`, `2m 3s`, or `3s`.
- The two estimated times are left out when plymeld has no prediction.

### On every machine

- `VERSION` is plymeld's version, for example `0.20261026.0`. The line carries no date or time, so the same version,
  models, and values give the same file, byte for byte.
- To find the version, a tool reads the first line matching `^; generated by plymeld (\S+)$` among the first ten
  lines.
- When the machine's screen shows a picture of the file, it follows the header (on most machines, right after the
  `total layer number` line):
  `; THUMBNAIL_BLOCK_START`, then for each picture `; thumbnail begin WIDTHxHEIGHT LENGTH`, the PNG in base64 (78
  characters a line), and `; thumbnail end`; then `; THUMBNAIL_BLOCK_END`. `LENGTH` is the number of base64
  characters.

## The source block

The last lines of the file: what it was made from. `plymeld slice --from FILE` reads it to slice the file again.

```
; PLYMELD_SOURCE_BLOCK_START
; format = "1"
; # ...
; plymeld = "VERSION"
; model = "NAME"  # BYTES bytes, sha256 HASH
; config: COUNT values (...), sha256 HASH
; used, yours: N value(s)
; KEY = VALUE  # SOURCE
; used, plymeld's: N value(s)
; KEY = VALUE  # SOURCE
; other, yours: N value(s)
; KEY = VALUE  # SOURCE
; other, plymeld's: N value(s)
; KEY = VALUE  # SOURCE
; plan: ...
; PLAN LINE
; PLYMELD_SOURCE_BLOCK_END
```

In this order:

1. `; PLYMELD_SOURCE_BLOCK_START`.
2. `; format = "1"`: the format's number. It goes up when a change would make a reader of the older format misread
   a file. A line kind added that older readers can skip does not raise it. A reader refuses a number it does not
   know.
3. Comment lines, `; # ...`: an explanation for people. Readers skip every line that starts with `; #`.
4. `; plymeld = "VERSION"`: the version that wrote the file.
5. One line per model file, in the order given: `; model = "NAME"  # BYTES bytes, sha256 HASH`. `NAME` is the file's
   name without its folder, `BYTES` its size, and `HASH` the SHA-256 of its contents in lowercase hex.
6. `; config: COUNT values (...), sha256 HASH`: `COUNT` values follow in four groups. `HASH` is the SHA-256 of the
   four groups' lines (headings included) as written here, each line ending in a newline, in UTF-8.
7. The four groups, always all four and in this order, each a heading and then its values:
   - `; used, yours: N value(s)`: values the print read, from your config files or the command line;
   - `; used, plymeld's: N value(s)`: values the print read, from plymeld's own (bundled) config;
   - `; other, yours: N value(s)`: the rest of yours;
   - `; other, plymeld's: N value(s)`: the rest of plymeld's.

   Each value line is `; KEY = VALUE  # SOURCE`, sorted by `KEY`:
   - `KEY` is the config path, for example `hardware.machine.m.build.x`.
   - `VALUE` is a TOML string, `"..."`, or an array of them, `["...", "..."]`. A value that starts with `!` carries the
     config file's keep mark, as it was written there.
   - `SOURCE` is where the value was set: a file's name and line (`machine.toml:12`), plymeld's own file
     (`bundled 00_defaults.toml:40`), or the command line.

   Left out: a machine's connection (its address and where its credentials are), the hardware this print does not
   use, and the folders of every source.
8. `; plan: ...`, then the plan: the decisions the file was sliced with, as `plymeld plan -o` writes them. Each line of
   the plan follows `; `; an empty one is `;` alone.
9. `; PLYMELD_SOURCE_BLOCK_END`.

### Reading it

- Removing `; ` from the start of each value line in step 7 leaves a line of TOML. The same goes for the plan's
  lines, which together make one TOML file.
- The block is the last part of the file. A tool finds it by its first and last lines.
